newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end sharply lower, seen steadying.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end sharply lower, seen steadying.

text.p: Argentine stocks took a heavy hit Monday on currency jitters in Brazil but were seen finding their feet by mid-week, dealers said.

"The market needed some bad news to latch onto in order to perform a correction, and it came in the form of the heavy drop in Brazil on talk of a possible devaluation like the recent one in Thailand," said Miguel Daneri at traders Boston Securities.
The blue-chip MerVal index dropped 1.7 percent to 836.14, its heaviest fall in nearly three months, and pared gains so far in July to 3.5 percent.
"Today's fall was pretty broad-based and it can be blamed on the devaluation fears in Brazil," said Augusto Milou at traders Galicia Valores.
Traders said the bolsa's undertone remained firm and the market would try to bounce back to 850 by Wednesday.
"If U.S. economic indicators due tomorrow and Wednesday are good the bolsa should have enough support to level out," dealer said.
The broad market index closed off 1.3 percent in the session, with losers beating winners 43 to 20 and 13 stocks closing flat.

Floor volume fell to 20.1 million pesos from 36.7 million pesos Friday, while over-the-counter turnover dwindled to just 31.5 million pesos from an already weak tally of 61.9 million Friday. "It's always a good to see volume shrink when prices fall -- it means sellers aren't out in force," a dealer said.

The heaviest main-tier losers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, construction stock Polledo and holding company Comercial del Plata, which tumbled 6.3 percent, 5.7 percent and 4.3 percent, respectively. The strongest winner was holding company Garovaglio, which lost 1.5 percent.
